newsitem.title: UK: BAA launches duty free retail company.
newsitem.headline: BAA launches duty free retail company.

text.p: Airport operator BAA Plc on Monday launched a new subsiduary, World Duty Free Ltd, in a drive to capture a significant share of the $20 billion world market for duty- and tax-free goods.
The company said in a statement it expected to announce shortly the appointment of a top duty free retail expert as chief executive of World Duty Free.

World Duty Free will take over the duty-free outlets at BAA's airports which are run on its behalf by Nuance, formerly the international duty-free arm of British retailer Allders and now owned by Swissair.

BAA tried to buy Nuance earlier this year but was outbid by Swissair. Last week BAA announced it would not renew the Nuance management contracts due to expire next year for London Heathrow Terminal 2, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Stansted and Southampton.
"We obviously think we can do it better," BAA's finance director told Reuters in an interview on Monday.
"But really the issue is to take control of what we believe is our business and get the synergies and economies of scale."

Walls said the cost of taking over the business would be relatively small. "In terms of cash it's not a big deal at all," he said. "We already have warehouses and computer systems...It's more a logistical exercise to get everything in place so that when the Swissair contracts run out we take over seamlessly."

BAA said its plans for World Duty Free included a series of new initiatives, including the opening of Studio 55, the first airport shop in the world for Japanese travellers and a store devoted to perfumes.
It currently has a five percent share of the world market for duty- and tax-free sales. The leader, DFS, has 14 percent.

"We have for some time made it clear we have international ambitions in a market in which we have as much expertise and experience as any competitor," said BAA retail director Barry Gibson. "We intend to become a major player and will vigorously pursue every worthwhile opportunity, either on our own or with others."
Walls made it clear Nuance's remaining two contracts with BAA, for shops at Heathrow Terminal Four and Gatwick's South terminal, were unlikely to be renewed once they run out in 1999.
"What happens after that I would not want to speculate on at the moment but I can see which way the wind's blowing."
Walls said he was unable to say whether the airport catering and retailing group Alpha Airports would have a part to play in its new World Duty Free business.

There was some media speculation recently that BAA was interested in bidding for Alpha before a 25 percent stake was bought by Harrods store owner Mohammed Al Fayed, who already operates a concession at London Heathrow.
"It's difficult to answer that question right at the moment because of last week's events but yes, we will continue still to work with Alpha," he said.
"Clearly we need to understand what he (Al Fayed) has in mind and I have no doubt there will be conversations."
